g.text: WHY THE BUCKET MUST BE STABLE (and hashed, not random)
Math.random() < 0.5 would flip the feature on and off between page loads for the SAME user. A
deterministic hash of (featureId + ":" + userId) gives that user the same bucket forever, so the
experience is consistent AND the cohort is stable enough to measure an A/B result against.
Ramping 5% → 25% is also monotonic: bucket 3 was in at 5% and is still in at 25%, so nobody
ever loses a feature they already had. That property is free — and only because it is < and not ==.
Two real defects in THIS implementation:
1. Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is still negative ⇒ a negative bucket, which is < any percentage,
so that one unlucky user is ON even at 0%. Use Math.floorMod, or mask the sign bit.
2. String.hashCode() is not a hash function for bucketing — adjacent user ids land in adjacent
buckets, so a 1% rollout can quietly select a correlated slice of your users.
